courts.highest: Court of Assizes or Cour d'Assizes (consists of 1 judge; court hears primarily serious criminal cases)
courts.lower: courts of first instance; labor court
courts.note: appeals beyond the Court of Assizes are heard before the Court of Appeal or Cour d'Appel (in Noumea, New Caledonia) note 2: justice is generally administered under French law by the high administrator, but the 3 traditional kings administer customary law

gov.type: parliamentary democracy (Territorial Assembly); overseas collectivity of France

executive.chosen: French president elected by absolute-majority popular vote in 2 rounds, if needed, for a 5-year term (eligible for a second term); administrator superior appointed by the French president on the advice of the French Ministry of the Interior; the presidents of the Territorial Government and the Territorial Assembly elected by assembly members
executive.cabinet: Council of the Territory appointed by the administrator superior on the advice of the Territorial Assembly

gov.divisions: 3 administrative precincts (circonscriptions, singular - circonscription) Alo, Sigave, Uvea
